Re-derived. Boole: 1 - H(z_B) <= sum_k P(|Z_k| > z_B) = K x 2(1 - Phi(z_B)) = K x alpha/K = alpha, so H(z_B) >= 1 - alpha and h <= z_B. The replacement sentence 'Apart from a small gain that exists even under independence, the gain comes from dependence' is now true and agrees with the Remark's next sentence and with Lab 4's interpretation: by quadrature over the common factor, the limiting sup-t value for equicorrelated normals is 3.0160 at rho = 0, 2.9805 at 0.3 and 2.4794 at 0.9, never above the independence value (Sidak's inequality for Gaussian vectors), so everything beyond the 0.007 gain at rho = 0 is due to dependence. rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html lines 594-596 (equicorrelated normals are MTP2; their one-sided p-values are MTP2; Simes; Theorem 7.5)
rows.evidence: New in this round, re-derived. Claim: equicorrelated normal statistics with covariance (1 - rho) I + rho 1 1' of order m0 are MTP2, so the true-null p-values are MTP2 and satisfy the Simes inequality. (i) The inverse has diagonal d and off-diagonal -rho/((1-rho)(1-rho+m0 rho)) <= 0 (Sherman-Morrison; numerically equal for rho 0.3, 0.5, 0.8 and m0 5, 450). (ii) For u = x v y, v = x ^ y, the diagonal terms cancel because u_i^2 + v_i^2 = x_i^2 + y_i^2, giving log f(u) + log f(v) - log f(x) - log f(y) = (1/2) sum_{i != j} Q_ij (x_i x_j + y_i y_j - u_i u_j - v_i v_j): verified numerically to 1e-9 on 20,000 random pairs. (iii) The bracket is 0 when x_i - y_i and x_j - y_j share a sign and (x_i - y_i)(x_j - y_j) <= 0 otherwise; I checked both cases by hand (e.g. x_i >= y_i, x_j <= y_j gives u_i u_j + v_i v_j = x_i y_j + y_i x_j). With Q_ij <= 0 every term is >= 0, so f(u) f(v) >= f(x) f(y). (iv) p = 1 - Phi(z) is coordinatewise decreasing, so it swaps v and ^, the Jacobian is a product of one-coordinate factors whose values at the pair {a_i v b_i, a_i ^ b_i} multiply to the same product as at {a_i, b_i}, hence the p-values are MTP2. (v) MTP2 implies the Simes inequality: Lehmann and Romano's remark after Theorem 3.2, citing Sarkar and Chang (JASA 92(440) 1601-1608, 1997) and Sarkar (Ann. Statist. 26(2) 494-504, 1998, doi 10.1214/aos/1028144846; Crossref abstract: 'an analytical proof of ... [the Simes] conjecture' for MTP2 vectors). All steps are right for 0 <= rho < 1. FAILS on assumptions: the paragraph states the result for 'correlation rho >= 0' and concludes 'at every rho >= 0', but at rho = 1 the covariance is singular, (1 - rho) is zero in the displayed inverse, and the density argument does not apply (the conclusion is still true at rho = 1, where all true-null p-values coincide and the Simes probability is exactly alpha, but the proof given does not cover it).

Re-derived after the notation change. Dividing every constant of (3) by c = c(floor(gamma m) + 1) is (3) at alpha' = alpha/c (linear in alpha). Re-derived after the rename A -> D. If the original procedure makes no false rejection, the augmented procedure rejects R = R0 + D' with D' = min(D, m - R0) <= D, at most D' of them false; R = 0 gives FDP = 0; otherwise FDP <= D'/(R0 + D') <= D/(R0 + D) because x -> x/(R0 + x) is increasing; and D <= gamma R0/(1 - gamma) iff D (1 - gamma) <= gamma R0 iff D <= gamma (R0 + D), so FDP <= gamma. Hence {FDP > gamma} needs a false rejection by the original procedure: probability <= alpha. Correct, and the letters D, D' no longer clash with the active set A.
